arguments.issue: Can a single episode of self-induced intoxication resulting in toxic psychosis qualify as a 'mental disorder' under s. 16 Cr. C.?
arguments.claim: A single episode of intoxication causing toxic psychosis should be considered a 'mental disorder' under s. 16 Cr. C.
arguments.quote: According to him, any toxic psychosis, even one that results, as the trial judge found in this case, from a single episode of intoxication, must be considered a 'mental disorder' within the meaning of s. 16 Cr. C.
arguments.weak_spot: The other side will argue that self-induced intoxication cannot be equated with a mental disorder for criminal responsibility.

arguments.issue: Did the lower courts err by conflating the defences of self-induced intoxication and mental disorder, and misapplying s. 33.1 Cr. C.?
arguments.claim: The lower courts wrongly conflated self-induced intoxication with mental disorder and misapplied s. 33.1 Cr. C.
arguments.quote: The appellant thus contends that the Court of Appeal confused the defence of self‑induced intoxication with that of mental disorder under s. 16 Cr. C. in holding that s. 33.1 Cr. C. applied in this case.
arguments.weak_spot: The other side will argue that s. 33.1 Cr. C. was intended to prevent this defence in cases of self-induced intoxication.

arguments.issue: Does s. 33.1 Cr. C. limit the scope of the mental disorder defence under s. 16 Cr. C.?
arguments.claim: Section 33.1 Cr. C. does not limit the scope of the mental disorder defence under s. 16 Cr. C.
arguments.quote: In his opinion, this passage wrongly suggests that s. 33.1 Cr. C. limits the scope of the defence of not criminally responsible on account of mental disorder.
arguments.weak_spot: The other side will argue that Parliament intended s. 33.1 Cr. C. to restrict defences based on self-induced intoxication.

arguments.issue: What is the correct interpretation of Parliament's intent in enacting s. 33.1 Cr. C. regarding toxic psychosis and mental disorder?
arguments.claim: Parliament intended to bar self-induced intoxication as a defence, but not to exclude toxic psychosis as a mental disorder under s. 16 Cr. C.
arguments.quote: He points out that those dissenting judges had acknowledged that [translation] 'toxic psychosis remained a defence under s. 16' (A.F., at para. 74).
arguments.weak_spot: The other side will argue that the legislative intent was to prevent any defence based on self-induced intoxication, including toxic psychosis.
